title: Budget-capped utility versus information-gain probe selection
question: Does selecting probes by expected budget-capped posterior utility per acquisition work improve downstream hypothesis resolution over Shannon-information-per-work selection on the registered finite graph workload?
hypothesis: The budget-capped utility selector will weakly improve the expected probability that the target falls inside an eight-candidate terminal shortlist, but the magnitude may be small when the six-bit trace already nearly reaches its partition ceiling.

arms.name: information_per_work
arms.intervention: select the input row maximizing deterministic Shannon information gain per acquisition work

arms.name: budget_utility_per_work
arms.intervention: select the input row maximizing expected budget-capped posterior utility gain per acquisition work

endpoints.name: budget_capped_utility_delta_m512_b8
endpoints.role: primary — seed-level mean U_8 difference budget_utility_per_work minus information_per_work at M=512/B=8

endpoints.name: verified_success_delta_m512_b8
endpoints.role: secondary — seed-level exact-verifier success difference at M=512/B=8

endpoints.name: probe_work_delta_m512
endpoints.role: secondary — selected-action expected acquisition work difference

endpoints.name: selected_row_agreement
endpoints.role: secondary — fraction of paired tasks choosing the same probe row

endpoints.name: budget_utility
endpoints.role: secondary — U_B for each selected action

held_constant: same static 512-program evaluation library per seed

terminal_protocol.procedure: After the selected row is chosen without target identity, reveal the target evidence, form the exact compatible bucket, retain the first min(8,bucket_size) candidates in deterministic public order, and exact-verify those candidates against all 16 rows.

cost_model.acquisition_work: G-CASM graph execution work plus six activation-trace read units
cost_model.terminal_work: exact executor work over shortlisted candidates and all 16 rows
cost_model.equal_probe_count: both arms execute exactly one probe action; total acquisition work is separately reported

statistical_rule.per_seed_estimate: mean selected-action U_8 across the 32 paired tasks

leakage_rules: Both selectors see only candidate-predicted public activation traces and action descriptors.
Target identity and target index are never inputs to probe selection.
Realized target evidence is unavailable before action selection.
Verifier-only rows and labels are unavailable to probe selection.
No confirmatory result selects the utility definition, budget, or action space.

decision_rule.condition: Primary U_8 difference CI is positive at M=512/B=8.
decision_rule.licenses: Evidence that terminal-budget-aware utility is a better probe objective than Shannon information-per-work on the finite registered workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: A general submodularity guarantee, learned probe-policy superiority, or asymptotic optimality.

decision_rule.licenses: Shannon information and terminal-budget utility are effectively aligned on this trace workload; replacing the selector objective is not the immediate bottleneck.
On this finite workload, naive one-step U_B optimization does not improve the established information selector; multi-step lookahead or a different belief representation may be required.
decision_rule.does_not_license: A rejection of budget-aware objectives in general.
